title: Phase Coupler: hierarchical warmup synchronizer and token pathline reporter
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces a hierarchical warmup synchronizer and a phase-aware profiling serializer plus a token pathline reporter. Intended for benchmark lab use: no runtime API changes for customers; internal telemetry and perf tests benefit.
description:
Context and motivation: We observed persistent tail variance during multi-sequence warmups in the continuous-batcher experiments: single-primer warmup often left shard-local KV caches out of phase, producing amplified p95/p99 variability when sequences cross shard boundaries. This PR implements a hierarchical warmup synchronizer (the 'Phase Coupler') to coordinate warmup primers across node-local and cluster-level layers, and adds a phase-aware profiler serializer and a token-pathline reporter to make per-token warmup progress observable for benchmark analysis.

What this PR does (single continuous description): - Adds a hierarchical warmup synchronizer that runs at two levels: node-local primer orchestration and cluster-phase coupling. The coordinator exposes deterministic phase epochs so primers on different GPUs/instances align their KV cache priming windows. - Introduces phase markers in the profiling pipeline and a compact phase-aware serializer (protobuf + delta-encoded token timestamps) so phase boundaries are not lost in aggregation. - Implements a token pathline reporter that reconstructs per-request token-level warmup contribution (which tokens populated KV slabs, which primers were used) and exports CSVs and compressed parquet-like blobs for offline analysis. - Adds tests: unit tests for scheduler state machine, integration tests simulating multi-shard warmup with synthetic traffic, and an end-to-end benchmark job that demonstrates reduced tail variance in a controlled scenario. - Modifies the benchmark harness to optionally enable phase coupling via a toggle flag (enabled=false by default for backward compatibility). - Documentation: README describing tuning knobs and a short howto for analyzing token pathline outputs with the bench visualizer.

Checklist: - [x] Design review with infra and runtime (ENG-2142) - [x] Unit tests - [x] Integration warmup simulation - [x] End-to-end benchmark job + baseline comparison - [x] Documentation snippet and chart example - [x] CI green (after lint fix)

Commits (high level): - f2a1c9e: introduce phase-coupler core scheduler, state machine, and API stubs - 6b3d2a4: implement node-local primer coordinator and RPC shims - ab7c48d: add profiling phase markers and serializer proto definitions - 9e4d0f1: token pathline reporter (CSV + compressed blob writer) - 4b5e2c7: harness integration: toggles, flags, and e2e scenario - c2d7a88: tests and deterministic seed harness for CI - 8f9b33a: docs and bench visualizer example - 0a1b2c3: lint fix and CI configuration updates

Files changed (high level): - scheduler/phase_coupler.py (new) - scheduler/README.md (new design doc + knobs) - runtime/primer_coordinator.cc (updates to RPC handler) - profiling/phase_serializer.proto (new) - profiling/phase_serializer.go (new: serializer + tests) - reporters/token_pathline_reporter.go (new) - bench/harness/phase_coupler_job.yaml (new benchmark job) - bench/harness/tests/test_phase_alignment.py (new) - docs/bench-setup/phase-coupling.md (new) - ci/flakeignore (updated) - Makefile (targets for generating serializer bindings) - go.mod/go.sum updates

Why now: This provides an internal capability to deterministically prime KV caches across heterogeneous warmup primers and reduces spurious regression noise in tail latency benchmarks. It is intended to make our benchmark baselines more reproducible across CI runs and lab clusters.

Testing notes and results: The e2e bench job compares baseline (no coupling) vs enabled coupling on a 4-node cluster with mixed sequence lengths. Key results from local lab run (attached to the benchmark run artifact): baseline p95 = 312ms, baseline p99 = 680ms; with phase coupling p95 = 254ms (-19%), p99 = 498ms (-27%). End-to-end test included deterministic RNG seeds to remove sampling variance; see bench/harness/artifacts/phase-coupler-run-2026-02-28.tar.gz for traces.

Backward compatibility and rollout: Coupling is opt-in via the bench harness flag bench_phase_coupler_enabled (default false). We will roll out to nightly benchmarks for two weeks before enabling by default for regression runs. No customer-facing API change.

Observability: Adds two new metric families: bench.warmup.phase_epoch (gauge) and bench.warmup.token_primed_total (counter). Token pathline outputs include mapping to primer worker IDs and KV slab ids for root cause attribution.

Risks and mitigation: The synchronizer introduces extra coordination RPCs; for production runtime we keep this disabled by default and use it only within benchmark lab clusters. The serializer uses delta-encoding; if a bug corrupts phase markers it only affects offline analysis, not runtime serving.

Related work: builds on earlier primer orchestration efforts (ENG-1789) and denoiser tracing (ENG-1905).

Merge notes: Squash-merged after CI green and approvals.

review_thread: Jorge Ramirez: Design lgtm, but please show how you avoid head-of-line blocking when a node is slow to enter a phase.

Maya Patel: Good question — the coupler uses epoch leases and a sliding acceptance window; if a node misses an epoch we mark it as 'lagging' and allow shadow priming for up to 3 epochs before forcing catch-up. Added details in scheduler/README.md.
Lina Chen: Tests look solid. I asked for a small unit test covering delta-encoding edge-case (zero-length deltas).
Maya Patel: Added test for zero-length deltas in profiling/phase_serializer_test.go. CI triggered.
Omar Farouk: CI initially failed lint on scheduler/phase_coupler.py (unused import). Once fixed, re-run passed. Approving now.
Jorge Ramirez: Approved after confirming metrics names and tags; note: consider a future opt-in for production-scale runs.

analysis_guidance: To analyze token pathlines: unpack the compressed blobs with tools/report-decode, load CSV into bench-visualizer, filter by primer worker id and slab id, and overlay phase_epoch metric. See docs/bench-setup/phase-coupling.md for example commands.
